meta.title: Oncora Nexus curated breast oncology knowledge cards
meta.description: Authored evidence summaries that condense widely adopted standards of care and landmark trials. They are written for retrieval grounding, are not a substitute for the source guideline, and must be checked against the current NICE, ESMO, ASCO or local MDT protocol before any clinical use.
meta.licence: CC BY 4.0, authored for this project

cards.title: Nottingham Prognostic Index
cards.body: The Nottingham Prognostic Index (NPI) combines three pathology variables: 0.2 multiplied by invasive tumour size in centimetres, plus histological grade (1 to 3), plus lymph node stage (1 for node negative, 2 for one to three positive nodes, 3 for four or more positive nodes). Values of 3.4 or below indicate a good prognostic group, 3.41 to 5.4 a moderate group and above 5.4 a poor group. NPI underpins UK prognostic communication and is one of the variables available in the METABRIC cohort used by this platform.
references: Haybittle JL et al. Br J Cancer 1982
Blamey RW et al. Eur J Cancer 2007

cards.title: Oestrogen and progesterone receptor testing
cards.body: ER and PR status are assessed by immunohistochemistry on every invasive breast cancer. ASCO and CAP define a tumour as ER positive when at least 1 percent of tumour nuclei stain, and describe 1 to 10 percent staining as ER low positive, a group whose biology and endocrine sensitivity often resemble ER negative disease. UK laboratories commonly report the Allred score, where a total of 3 or more is positive. Receptor status determines eligibility for endocrine therapy and informs surrogate intrinsic subtype.
references: Allison KH et al. ASCO/CAP ER and PgR testing guideline, J Clin Oncol 2020
NICE NG101 Early and locally advanced breast cancer

cards.title: HER2 testing and the HER2 low category
cards.body: HER2 is scored by immunohistochemistry as 0, 1+, 2+ or 3+. A score of 3+ is HER2 positive, 2+ is equivocal and requires in situ hybridisation, and 0 or 1+ is HER2 negative for the purpose of HER2 targeted therapy in early disease. Tumours scoring 1+, or 2+ with a negative ISH result, are now described as HER2 low, which matters in the metastatic setting because trastuzumab deruxtecan improved survival in this group.
references: Wolff AC et al. ASCO/CAP HER2 testing guideline update, J Clin Oncol 2018 and 2023
Modi S et al. DESTINY-Breast04, N Engl J Med 2022

cards.title: Surrogate intrinsic subtypes from immunohistochemistry
cards.body: Gene expression profiling defines intrinsic subtypes (Luminal A, Luminal B, HER2 enriched, Basal like and Normal like, with Claudin low as an additional group). In routine practice a surrogate classification uses ER, PR, HER2 and Ki67 or grade: Luminal A like (ER and PR positive, HER2 negative, low proliferation), Luminal B like (ER positive with high proliferation or low PR, or HER2 positive), HER2 positive non luminal, and triple negative. Concordance between surrogate and expression based subtype is imperfect, which is why Oncora Nexus reports both and shows their disagreement.
references: Goldhirsch A et al. St Gallen consensus, Ann Oncol 2013
Parker JS et al. PAM50, J Clin Oncol 2009

cards.title: TNM staging essentials
cards.body: The AJCC TNM system stages breast cancer by tumour size (T1 up to 20 mm, T2 over 20 mm to 50 mm, T3 over 50 mm, T4 any size with chest wall or skin involvement including inflammatory carcinoma), regional nodal status (N0 to N3) and distant metastasis (M0 or M1). The eighth edition added a prognostic stage group that incorporates grade, ER, PR and HER2 status. Stage IV disease is metastatic and is managed with treatment aims of disease control and quality of life rather than cure in most patients.
references: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual, 8th edition

cards.title: Adjuvant endocrine therapy for premenopausal women
cards.body: For premenopausal women with ER positive early breast cancer, tamoxifen for five years is the standard baseline, with extension to ten years considered for those at higher risk of recurrence. In women at sufficiently high risk to warrant chemotherapy, adding ovarian function suppression to tamoxifen or to an aromatase inhibitor improved disease free survival in the SOFT and TEXT trials, at the cost of more menopausal side effects.
references: Francis PA et al. SOFT and TEXT, N Engl J Med 2018
Davies C et al. ATLAS, Lancet 2013
NICE NG101

cards.title: Adjuvant endocrine therapy for postmenopausal women
cards.body: Aromatase inhibitors (anastrozole, letrozole, exemestane) reduce recurrence more than tamoxifen in postmenopausal women with ER positive early breast cancer, as shown in the EBCTCG patient level meta analysis. NICE recommends an aromatase inhibitor as initial therapy for postmenopausal women at medium or high risk, with tamoxifen an option for low risk disease or when an aromatase inhibitor is not tolerated. Extended therapy beyond five years is discussed when the residual recurrence risk is meaningful.
references: EBCTCG, Lancet 2015
NICE NG101

cards.title: Managing endocrine therapy toxicity and adherence
cards.body: Aromatase inhibitors commonly cause arthralgia, vaginal dryness and accelerated bone loss, so a baseline bone density scan is recommended. Tamoxifen increases the risk of venous thromboembolism and endometrial cancer and can worsen vasomotor symptoms. Non adherence affects a substantial minority of patients and is associated with worse outcomes, so switching agents, symptom management and structured follow up are preferred to discontinuation.
references: NICE NG101
Hershman DL et al. J Clin Oncol 2010

cards.title: Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors in high risk HR positive disease
cards.body: In the monarchE trial, two years of abemaciclib added to endocrine therapy improved invasive disease free survival in HR positive, HER2 negative, node positive early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence (four or more positive nodes, or one to three nodes with grade 3 disease or a tumour of at least 5 cm). NATALEE showed benefit for three years of ribociclib with a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor in a broader stage II and III population. Diarrhoea, neutropenia and, for ribociclib, QT prolongation and liver toxicity require monitoring.
references: Johnston SRD et al. monarchE, J Clin Oncol 2020 and 2023
Slamon D et al. NATALEE, N Engl J Med 2024

cards.title: Genomic recurrence scores and chemotherapy decisions
cards.body: In HR positive, HER2 negative early breast cancer, multigene assays refine the decision about adjuvant chemotherapy. In TAILORx (node negative), women with an Oncotype DX recurrence score of 11 to 25 derived no overall benefit from chemotherapy, although women aged 50 or younger with scores of 16 to 25 showed some benefit. In RxPONDER (one to three positive nodes, score 25 or below), postmenopausal women did not benefit from chemotherapy whereas premenopausal women did. MINDACT validated the 70 gene signature for de escalation in clinically high, genomically low risk disease.
references: Sparano JA et al. TAILORx, N Engl J Med 2018
Kalinsky K et al. RxPONDER, N Engl J Med 2021
Cardoso F et al. MINDACT, N Engl J Med 2016

cards.title: Adjuvant and neoadjuvant chemotherapy backbones
cards.body: Standard chemotherapy for early breast cancer combines an anthracycline and a taxane, for example epirubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel or docetaxel, with dose dense scheduling offering a modest additional benefit in higher risk disease. Anthracycline free regimens such as docetaxel and cyclophosphamide are used when cardiac risk is a concern. The EBCTCG meta analyses show that the proportional benefit of chemotherapy is broadly similar across subgroups, so absolute benefit depends on baseline risk.
references: EBCTCG, Lancet 2012 and 2019

cards.title: Neoadjuvant therapy and pathological complete response
cards.body: Systemic therapy before surgery is preferred for most HER2 positive and triple negative tumours above about 2 cm or node positive, because the pathological response guides adjuvant therapy and can enable breast conserving surgery. Pathological complete response (no residual invasive disease in breast and nodes) is strongly associated with better event free survival in these subtypes, while residual disease identifies patients who benefit from escalation.
references: Cortazar P et al. CTNeoBC pooled analysis, Lancet 2014
ESMO Early Breast Cancer Guideline 2024

cards.title: Adjuvant trastuzumab and dual HER2 blockade
cards.body: Trastuzumab given with chemotherapy for HER2 positive early breast cancer roughly halves recurrence risk and is standard for tumours larger than about 1 cm or node positive disease. Twelve months is the international standard, and the UK PERSEPHONE trial found six months non inferior for disease free survival. Adding pertuzumab (APHINITY) gave a small invasive disease free survival gain concentrated in node positive disease. Neoadjuvant regimens commonly use pertuzumab, trastuzumab and a taxane with or without carboplatin.
references: Earl HM et al. PERSEPHONE, Lancet 2019
von Minckwitz G et al. APHINITY, N Engl J Med 2017

cards.title: Residual disease after neoadjuvant HER2 therapy
cards.body: For patients with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy and HER2 targeted therapy, the KATHERINE trial showed that switching to trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) for 14 cycles reduced the risk of invasive recurrence or death by about half compared with continuing trastuzumab, with an overall survival benefit on longer follow up.
references: von Minckwitz G et al. KATHERINE, N Engl J Med 2019
Geyer CE et al. N Engl J Med 2025

cards.title: Cardiac monitoring during HER2 targeted therapy
cards.body: Trastuzumab can cause a usually reversible reduction in left ventricular ejection fraction. Baseline assessment of LVEF by echocardiography or MUGA and repeat assessment around every three months during treatment is standard. Treatment is typically paused when LVEF falls below 50 percent with a significant drop from baseline, and cardio oncology input is sought. Prior anthracycline exposure increases the risk.
references: NICE NG101
ESC Cardio Oncology Guidelines 2022

cards.title: Metastatic HER2 positive breast cancer sequencing
cards.body: First line treatment for metastatic HER2 positive disease is pertuzumab, trastuzumab and a taxane (CLEOPATRA), which produced a median overall survival of over 56 months. Trastuzumab deruxtecan is the preferred second line therapy after DESTINY-Breast03 showed superior progression free and overall survival versus T-DM1. Tucatinib with trastuzumab and capecitabine (HER2CLIMB) is active including in patients with brain metastases.
references: Swain SM et al. CLEOPATRA, N Engl J Med 2015
Cortes J et al. DESTINY-Breast03, N Engl J Med 2022
Murthy RK et al. HER2CLIMB, N Engl J Med 2020

cards.title: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy for early triple negative breast cancer
cards.body: For stage II and III triple negative breast cancer, KEYNOTE-522 showed that adding pembrolizumab to neoadjuvant carboplatin and paclitaxel followed by anthracycline and cyclophosphamide, then continuing pembrolizumab after surgery, improved pathological complete response, event free survival and overall survival. Immune related adverse events, including endocrinopathies, need structured monitoring.
references: Schmid P et al. KEYNOTE-522, N Engl J Med 2020, 2022 and 2024

cards.title: Post neoadjuvant escalation in triple negative and BRCA associated disease
cards.body: Patients with residual invasive triple negative disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy benefit from adjuvant capecitabine (CREATE-X). For germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 carriers with high risk HER2 negative early breast cancer, one year of adjuvant olaparib improved invasive disease free and overall survival in OlympiA, so germline testing at diagnosis is important for treatment planning.
references: Masuda N et al. CREATE-X, N Engl J Med 2017
Tutt ANJ et al. OlympiA, N Engl J Med 2021

cards.title: Metastatic triple negative breast cancer
cards.body: In metastatic triple negative breast cancer with PD-L1 combined positive score of 10 or more, first line pembrolizumab with chemotherapy improved overall survival (KEYNOTE-355). Sacituzumab govitecan, a TROP2 antibody drug conjugate, improved survival in previously treated disease (ASCENT). PARP inhibitors olaparib and talazoparib are options for germline BRCA carriers.
references: Cortes J et al. KEYNOTE-355, N Engl J Med 2022
Bardia A et al. ASCENT, N Engl J Med 2021
Robson M et al. OlympiAD, N Engl J Med 2017

cards.title: First line therapy for HR positive, HER2 negative metastatic disease
cards.body: An aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant combined with a CDK4/6 inhibitor (palbociclib, ribociclib or abemaciclib) is the standard first line approach for most patients, roughly doubling progression free survival compared with endocrine therapy alone, and ribociclib has demonstrated an overall survival benefit across the MONALEESA trials. Premenopausal women receive ovarian function suppression alongside. Chemotherapy first is reserved for visceral crisis or rapidly progressing disease.
references: Hortobagyi GN et al. MONALEESA-2, N Engl J Med 2022
Finn RS et al. PALOMA-2, N Engl J Med 2016
ESMO Metastatic Breast Cancer Living Guideline

cards.title: Biomarker directed therapy after progression on CDK4/6 inhibition
cards.body: Testing for PIK3CA, AKT1, PTEN and ESR1 alterations guides second line choices. Alpelisib (SOLAR-1) and capivasertib (CAPItello-291) with fulvestrant improve progression free survival in tumours with relevant PI3K pathway alterations, inavolisib combinations are available for PIK3CA mutated disease, and the oral SERD elacestrant improved outcomes in ESR1 mutated disease (EMERALD). Everolimus with exemestane remains an option. Hyperglycaemia and rash are notable toxicities of PI3K pathway agents.
references: Andre F et al. SOLAR-1, N Engl J Med 2019
Turner NC et al. CAPItello-291, N Engl J Med 2023
Bidard FC et al. EMERALD, J Clin Oncol 2022

cards.title: Antibody drug conjugates for HER2 low and endocrine refractory disease
cards.body: Trastuzumab deruxtecan improved progression free and overall survival versus physician choice chemotherapy in HER2 low metastatic breast cancer after prior chemotherapy (DESTINY-Breast04), and DESTINY-Breast06 extended benefit to chemotherapy naive HER2 low and HER2 ultralow disease after endocrine therapy. Interstitial lung disease is the key toxicity and needs prompt recognition. Sacituzumab govitecan is also active in endocrine resistant HR positive disease (TROPiCS-02).
references: Modi S et al. DESTINY-Breast04, N Engl J Med 2022
Bardia A et al. DESTINY-Breast06, N Engl J Med 2024
Rugo HS et al. TROPiCS-02, Lancet 2023

cards.title: Breast conserving surgery versus mastectomy
cards.body: Breast conserving surgery followed by whole breast radiotherapy gives overall survival equivalent to mastectomy for suitable early breast cancers, as shown by long term follow up of NSABP B-06 and the Milan trial. Clear margins (no tumour on ink for invasive cancer) are the accepted standard. Mastectomy is chosen for multicentric disease, unfavourable breast to tumour ratio, contraindication to radiotherapy, or patient preference, with immediate or delayed reconstruction offered.
references: Fisher B et al. NSABP B-06, N Engl J Med 2002
Veronesi U et al. N Engl J Med 2002
NICE NG101

cards.title: Axillary management and de escalation
cards.body: Sentinel lymph node biopsy is standard for clinically node negative disease. In ACOSOG Z0011, women with T1 or T2 tumours, one or two positive sentinel nodes, breast conserving surgery and whole breast radiotherapy had no survival detriment when axillary dissection was omitted. AMAROS showed axillary radiotherapy controls the axilla as well as dissection with less lymphoedema. These findings support avoiding axillary clearance in many patients.
references: Giuliano AE et al. ACOSOG Z0011, JAMA 2017
Donker M et al. AMAROS, Lancet Oncol 2014

cards.title: Whole breast radiotherapy fractionation
cards.body: After breast conserving surgery, whole breast radiotherapy reduces local recurrence and breast cancer mortality (EBCTCG). The UK FAST-Forward trial showed 26 Gy in five fractions over one week was non inferior to 40 Gy in 15 fractions for local control with similar normal tissue effects, and NICE recommends 26 Gy in five fractions for whole breast or chest wall radiotherapy without nodal irradiation. A tumour bed boost is considered for higher risk of local recurrence.
references: Murray Brunt A et al. FAST-Forward, Lancet 2020
EBCTCG, Lancet 2011
NICE NG101

cards.title: Omitting radiotherapy in low risk older women
cards.body: For women aged 65 or over with small, node negative, HR positive tumours treated with breast conserving surgery and endocrine therapy, omitting radiotherapy increased ipsilateral recurrence modestly but did not affect overall survival in PRIME II. NICE supports discussing omission of radiotherapy with patients at very low risk of local recurrence who will take endocrine therapy for five years.
references: Kunkler IH et al. PRIME II, N Engl J Med 2023
NICE NG101

cards.title: Postmastectomy and nodal radiotherapy
cards.body: Postmastectomy radiotherapy to the chest wall is recommended for four or more involved axillary nodes or involved resection margins, and is considered for one to three involved nodes when other high risk features are present. Regional nodal irradiation reduced distant recurrence in node positive disease in the MA.20 and EORTC 22922 trials, at the cost of more lymphoedema and pneumonitis.
references: EBCTCG, Lancet 2014
Whelan TJ et al. MA.20, N Engl J Med 2015
Poortmans PM et al. EORTC 22922, N Engl J Med 2015

cards.title: Adjuvant bisphosphonates
cards.body: In postmenopausal women (natural or induced), adjuvant bisphosphonates such as zoledronic acid or oral clodronate reduce bone recurrence and breast cancer mortality, according to the EBCTCG meta analysis. NICE recommends offering them to postmenopausal women with node positive invasive breast cancer and considering them for node negative disease at high risk. Dental review before starting reduces the risk of osteonecrosis of the jaw.
references: EBCTCG, Lancet 2015
NICE NG101

cards.title: Chemotherapy induced nausea, neutropenia and neuropathy
cards.body: Anthracycline and cyclophosphamide regimens are highly emetogenic and warrant a neurokinin 1 receptor antagonist, a 5HT3 antagonist and dexamethasone. Dose dense regimens require granulocyte colony stimulating factor support. Taxane induced peripheral neuropathy is common and may be persistent, and dose modification is the main management strategy. Neutropenic sepsis is a medical emergency requiring antibiotics within one hour.
references: MASCC/ESMO antiemetic guideline 2023
NICE CG151 Neutropenic sepsis

cards.title: Lymphoedema after breast cancer treatment
cards.body: Lymphoedema affects roughly one in five women after axillary dissection and less commonly after sentinel node biopsy alone or axillary radiotherapy. Early referral to a lymphoedema service, compression, skin care and exercise are the basis of management. Progressive resistance exercise does not increase lymphoedema risk and is encouraged.
references: DiSipio T et al. Lancet Oncol 2013
Schmitz KH et al. N Engl J Med 2009

cards.title: Exercise, psychological support and quality of life
cards.body: Randomised trials consistently show that supervised aerobic and resistance exercise during and after treatment improves fatigue, physical function and quality of life. Cognitive behavioural approaches reduce anxiety, depression and insomnia, and structured psychosocial support is recommended at diagnosis and at transitions in care. Hot flushes can be reduced with cognitive behavioural therapy or non hormonal drugs such as some SSRIs or SNRIs, though strong CYP2D6 inhibitors should be avoided with tamoxifen.
references: Campbell KL et al. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2019
NICE NG101

cards.title: Germline genetic testing
cards.body: NICE recommends offering BRCA1 and BRCA2 testing when the combined probability of a pathogenic variant is 10 percent or more, and testing at diagnosis is increasingly offered to all patients with triple negative breast cancer under 60 or those eligible for PARP inhibitor therapy. Moderate penetrance genes include PALB2, CHEK2 and ATM. Results affect surgical choices, adjuvant olaparib eligibility and cascade testing of relatives.
references: NICE CG164 Familial breast cancer
Tutt ANJ et al. OlympiA, N Engl J Med 2021

cards.title: Risk reduction for women at increased familial risk
cards.body: For women at moderate or high familial risk, NICE recommends offering tamoxifen to premenopausal women and anastrozole to postmenopausal women for five years as chemoprevention, unless contraindicated, with raloxifene as an alternative for postmenopausal women with a uterus. Enhanced surveillance with annual MRI is offered to BRCA carriers from age 30, and risk reducing mastectomy and salpingo oophorectomy are discussed with carriers.
references: NICE CG164
Cuzick J et al. IBIS-II, Lancet 2014

cards.title: Population screening and triple assessment
cards.body: The NHS Breast Screening Programme invites women from age 50 up to their 71st birthday for mammography every three years. Symptomatic patients are assessed with triple assessment: clinical examination, imaging (mammography and ultrasound, with ultrasound alone often used under 40), and core needle biopsy. Digital breast tomosynthesis and contrast enhanced techniques improve detection in dense breasts.
references: NHS Breast Screening Programme
NICE NG12 Suspected cancer recognition and referral

cards.title: Ductal carcinoma in situ
cards.body: DCIS is a non invasive proliferation that may progress to invasive cancer. Standard treatment is breast conserving surgery with clear margins, usually followed by radiotherapy, which halves ipsilateral recurrence without a clear survival effect, or mastectomy for extensive disease. Endocrine therapy reduces recurrence in ER positive DCIS. Active monitoring of low risk DCIS is being evaluated in trials such as LORIS and COMET.
references: EBCTCG DCIS overview, J Natl Cancer Inst Monogr 2010
NICE NG101

cards.title: Breast cancer in older adults
cards.body: Treatment decisions for older adults should incorporate a geriatric assessment of comorbidity, function and life expectancy rather than chronological age alone. Primary endocrine therapy without surgery can be appropriate for frail women with ER positive disease. Older women are under represented in trials, so tools such as PREDICT Breast and shared decision making are particularly important.
references: Wildiers H et al. SIOG and EUSOMA recommendations, Lancet Oncol 2012
Age Gap study, Health Technol Assess 2022

cards.title: Young women, fertility and pregnancy
cards.body: Women of reproductive age should be offered fertility counselling and preservation before gonadotoxic chemotherapy, and ovarian suppression with a GnRH agonist during chemotherapy may reduce premature ovarian insufficiency. The POSITIVE trial suggested that a temporary interruption of endocrine therapy to attempt pregnancy did not increase short term recurrence. During pregnancy, anthracycline based chemotherapy can be given in the second and third trimesters, whereas trastuzumab and tamoxifen are contraindicated.
references: Partridge AH et al. POSITIVE, N Engl J Med 2023
Lambertini M et al. ESMO fertility guideline 2020

cards.title: Male breast cancer
cards.body: Male breast cancer accounts for under 1 percent of breast cancers, is usually ER positive, and has a higher association with BRCA2. Treatment principles mirror those for women, but tamoxifen is the preferred adjuvant endocrine therapy; an aromatase inhibitor alone is not recommended without testicular suppression. All men with breast cancer should be offered genetic testing.
references: Hassett MJ et al. ASCO male breast cancer guideline, J Clin Oncol 2020

cards.title: Principles of metastatic breast cancer care
cards.body: Metastatic breast cancer is generally treatable but not curable, so treatment aims to extend survival while preserving quality of life. A biopsy of a metastasis is recommended where feasible to confirm receptor status, because ER, PR and HER2 can change. Sequential single agent therapy is usually preferred over combination chemotherapy outside visceral crisis, and early integration of palliative care improves symptom control.
references: Cardoso F et al. ABC6 consensus, Ann Oncol 2024
ESMO Metastatic Breast Cancer Living Guideline

cards.title: Bone and brain metastases
cards.body: Bone targeted agents (denosumab or zoledronic acid) reduce skeletal related events in patients with bone metastases, and single fraction radiotherapy is effective for painful bone metastases. Metastatic spinal cord compression is an emergency that requires immediate steroids and urgent imaging. Brain metastases are managed with stereotactic radiosurgery for limited disease, and HER2 directed systemic agents such as tucatinib and trastuzumab deruxtecan have intracranial activity.
references: Stopeck AT et al. J Clin Oncol 2010
NICE NG234 Spinal metastases and spinal cord compression

cards.title: Follow up after primary treatment
cards.body: NICE recommends annual mammography for five years after diagnosis, after which women aged 50 and over return to the screening programme. Routine imaging or tumour markers to look for metastases in asymptomatic patients is not recommended because it does not improve survival. Follow up focuses on adherence to endocrine therapy, late effects, bone health and psychological wellbeing.
references: NICE NG101

cards.title: PREDICT Breast and absolute benefit communication
cards.body: PREDICT Breast is a validated online tool, developed with UK registry data, that estimates overall survival at five, ten and fifteen years and the absolute benefit of adjuvant hormone therapy, chemotherapy, trastuzumab and bisphosphonates. Absolute rather than relative benefit should be used in shared decision making. Oncora Nexus survival estimates are research models and should be reconciled with validated tools such as PREDICT before discussion with patients.
references: Wishart GC et al. Breast Cancer Res 2010
NICE NG101

cards.title: Interpreting survival models and their limits
cards.body: Prognostic models trained on observational cohorts estimate risk under the treatments those patients received; they do not estimate the causal effect of choosing a different treatment. Discrimination (C index) and calibration must both be checked in an external population, and models trained on historical cohorts such as METABRIC (diagnosed 1977 to 2005) will overestimate risk for patients receiving contemporary therapy including HER2 targeted agents.
references: Steyerberg EW. Clinical Prediction Models, 2nd edition, 2019
Collins GS et al. TRIPOD+AI, BMJ 2024

cards.title: The multidisciplinary team meeting
cards.body: Every patient with breast cancer should have their diagnosis and treatment plan discussed at a multidisciplinary team meeting including surgery, oncology, radiology, pathology, specialist nursing and, where relevant, plastic surgery and genetics. Recommendations should record the evidence base, eligibility for clinical trials and the patient's preferences. Clinical trial participation should be considered for every patient where a suitable trial exists.
references: NICE NG101
Cancer Reform Strategy, Department of Health

cards.title: Clinical trial eligibility screening
cards.body: Eligibility criteria typically specify age, performance status (ECOG 0 to 1 or 0 to 2), receptor and HER2 status, disease setting, prior therapy limits, organ function thresholds, absence of active brain metastases and contraception requirements. Automated screening can rule trials in or out on structured criteria, but laboratory values and investigator judgement items must be verified manually, so a likely eligible result is a prompt for review rather than a determination.
references: ClinicalTrials.gov
Kim ES et al. ASCO and Friends of Cancer Research eligibility recommendations, J Clin Oncol 2017

cards.title: Inflammatory and locally advanced breast cancer
cards.body: Inflammatory breast cancer presents with rapid onset erythema and oedema of a third or more of the breast and is staged T4d. Standard care is trimodality treatment: neoadjuvant systemic therapy, modified radical mastectomy (skin sparing and immediate reconstruction are generally avoided), and postmastectomy radiotherapy. HER2 directed therapy and immunotherapy follow subtype specific indications.
references: Dawood S et al. International expert panel, Ann Oncol 2011
ESMO Early Breast Cancer Guideline 2024

cards.title: Lobular breast cancer
cards.body: Invasive lobular carcinoma accounts for about 10 to 15 percent of breast cancers, is characterised by loss of E cadherin (CDH1), is usually ER positive and grade 2, and can be difficult to detect on mammography, so MRI is often used for extent assessment. Lobular tumours respond less to neoadjuvant chemotherapy and are prone to late recurrence and unusual metastatic sites such as the peritoneum and gastrointestinal tract.
references: McCart Reed AE et al. Nat Rev Clin Oncol 2021

cards.title: Extended adjuvant endocrine therapy
cards.body: Recurrence risk in ER positive disease persists for at least twenty years after diagnosis, and is higher with larger tumours and more involved nodes. Extending tamoxifen to ten years (ATLAS, aTTom) or adding an aromatase inhibitor after five years of tamoxifen (MA.17) reduces late recurrence. The benefit of extension must be balanced against cumulative toxicity, and is greatest for node positive disease.
references: Pan H et al. EBCTCG, N Engl J Med 2017
Goss PE et al. MA.17, N Engl J Med 2003
